name: Clear + Brilliant

lead: Clear + Brilliant is a gentle fractional laser used as an entry-level skin refresh for tone, texture and early aging signs, usually in a series of sessions.
Published support is limited to small studies.

paras: Two wavelengths (1440 and 1927 nm) create tiny zones of thermal injury while leaving surrounding skin intact, prompting collagen remodeling and skin turnover [1].
Mild redness is reported to resolve quickly [1]. As a laser procedure it carries general fractional-laser risks, and results are described as lasting months.

lead: Clear + Brilliant is a non-ablative fractional laser by Solta Medical, marketed as a gentle, low-downtime resurfacing option for early signs of aging, with an original 1440 nm handpiece and a 1927 nm Perméa handpiece [1]. It is often described as a "baby Fraxel" and is positioned as preventive skin maintenance [1].

Published human data are limited to small trials: registered studies cover photoaging, periorbital rejuvenation and melasma in groups of 14 to 40 people [2][3][4][5]. Claims of high satisfaction and millions of treatments come from manufacturer-oriented descriptions rather than from controlled trials [1].

paras: According to Grokipedia, Clear + Brilliant received FDA 510(k) clearance in May 2011, the Perméa handpiece was added in 2012, and the dual-wavelength Clear + Brilliant Touch launched in the US in 2021 [1]. That page is AI-generated and was not independently verified.

The device delivers fractional laser energy that creates microscopic treatment zones without removing the epidermal surface, which is said to trigger wound healing, collagen production and cell turnover [1].
Grokipedia reports mild redness resolving within hours to a day and a typical series of four to six sessions [1]. Proponents describe improved tone, texture, radiance and pore appearance [1].

Registered studies include a trial of combination versus laser-only treatment for photoaging (n=14) [2], a study of the 1440/1927 nm Touch device in photoaging (n=28) [3], a 1927 nm periorbital rejuvenation study (n=20) [4], and a study combining 1927 nm laser with topical cysteamine for melasma (n=20) [5]. Outcome data from these registrations are not summarised here.

timeline.event: Clear + Brilliant Touch launched in the US [1].
